Problems with this:

The core problem: You’re mixing “what to do” with “how to do it”. The
PaymentProcessor
shouldn’t care about PayPal’s API details. It just needs to know “I can call

blocks.html: 3. Code that actually uses it
blocks.text: 3. Code that actually uses it

blocks.html: from abc import ABC, abstractmethod # 1. Strategy Interface class PaymentStrategy(ABC): @abstractmethod def pay(self, amount): pass # 2. Concrete Strategies - each is one algorithm class CreditCardStrategy(PaymentStrategy): def __init__(self, card_number): self.card_number = card_number def pay(self, amount): print(f"Charging ${amount} to card ending {self.card_number[-4:]}") class PayPalStrategy(PaymentStrategy): def __init__(self, email): self.email = email def pay(self, amount): print(f"Paying ${amount} via PayPal account {self.email}") class UPIStrategy(PaymentStrategy): def __init__(self, upi_id): self.upi_id = upi_id def pay(self, amount): print(f"Paying ${amount} using UPI ID {self.upi_id}") # 3. Context - doesn't care which strategy it uses class PaymentProcessor: def __init__(self, strategy: PaymentStrategy): self.strategy = strategy def set_strategy(self, strategy: PaymentStrategy): """This is the key: swap strategy at runtime""" self.strategy = strategy def checkout(self, amount): # Delegate the work to the strategy self.strategy.pay(amount) # Usage: switch behavior at runtime order_amount = 1200 processor = PaymentProcessor(CreditCardStrategy("1234-5678-9012-3456")) processor.checkout(order_amount) # Charging $1200 to card ending 3456 # User changes mind, picks PayPal instead processor.set_strategy(PayPalStrategy("user@example.com")) processor.checkout(order_amount) # Paying $1200 via PayPal account user@example.com
